rationale: C12 is a direct and material drafting template. The child repeats its two-agreement framework, the same sequence of recitals concerning the Annecy accession agreement and the Cuban exclusive agreement, the same machinery for activating previously withheld Schedule XX concessions when a named government becomes a contracting party, and the same two-part operative structure. The child adapts C12 by substituting Uruguay and December 16, 1953, changing the tariff items, and adding a cattle-and-beef proviso. C19 and C20 are later variations in the same proclamation series, but C12 most closely matches the child's language and operative architecture.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the trade agreement for accession ... has been signed by the said Government under such circumstances that it will enter into force for such Government, and such Government will become a contracting party ... on December 16, 1953
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the trade agreement for accession ... has been signed by the Government of the Kingdom of Greece under such circumstances that it will enter into force for such Government, and such Government will become a contracting party ... on March 9, 1950
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive recital language is reused almost verbatim, with Uruguay and the effective date substituted for Greece and its date.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the application of each of the concessions provided for in Part I of Schedule XX in Annex A ... which were withheld from application in accordance with paragraph 4 ... is required or appropriate to carry out
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the application of each of the concessions provided for in Part I of Schedule XX in Annex A ... which were withheld from application in accordance with paragraph 4 ... is required or appropriate to carry out
shared_material.explanation: The child reproduces the same legal mechanism and highly specific formulation for releasing withheld Annecy concessions.

shared_material.child_excerpt: PART I To the end that the said trade agreement for accession ... may be carried out, the identification of each of the concessions ... shall ... be included in the list set forth in the ninth recital of the said proclamation of December 22, 1949
shared_material.parent_excerpt: PART I To the end that the said trade agreement for accession ... may be carried out, the identification of each of the concessions ... shall ... be included in the list set forth in the ninth recital of the said proclamation of December 22, 1949
shared_material.explanation: The principal operative provision follows C12's wording and administrative machinery nearly verbatim.

shared_material.child_excerpt: PART II To the end that the said exclusive trade agreement ... may be carried out, the list set forth in the ninth recital of the said proclamation of January 1, 1948 ... shall ... be further amended by deleting therefrom Item 1530 (a)
shared_material.parent_excerpt: PART II To the end that the said exclusive trade agreement ... may be carried out, the list set forth in the ninth recital of the said proclamation of January 1, 1948 ... shall ... be further amended by deleting therefrom the Item 328
shared_material.explanation: The child preserves the second operative part's structure and simply replaces the affected tariff item and date.
